newsitem.title: GREECE: Serb telcom buy will not harm domestic plans - OTE.
newsitem.headline: Serb telcom buy will not harm domestic plans - OTE.

text.p: OTE telecom said on Monday the cost of its purchase of a 20 percent stake in Serbia Telekom would be met from its own resources and would not jeopardise its ambitious domestic modernisation programme.
OTE said it would pay 675 million marks for its stake with Italy's telecoms holding company Stet buying 29 percent of Serbia Telekom for 893 million marks.

"OTE will pay the Serbian government 543 million marks immediately, while a further 132 million marks will be paid in January 1998," George Skarpelis, general manager of OTE's telecoms systems told Reuters.
The January 1998 instalment will not be deemed payable before a joint venture between Telekom Srbija, Stet and OTE has started implementing a cellular network in New Serbia, he added.
Telekom Srbija is a holder of a 20-year licence for a GSM mobile telephony network, enjoying a monopoly in its first eight years of operation.
It will control 51 percent of the mobile telephony provider's capital, with Stet and OTE commanding 29 percent and 20 percent, respectively.
OTE holds a call option to raise its stake in the mobile telephony provider from 20 percent to 24 percent.
OTE's management told Reuters it would meet the cost of the acquisition by equity set aside between 1995 and 2000 for this purpose.
"The cost of the deal will be entirely met by own-equity," Skarpelis said.
OTE has been setting aside funds for such corporate moves since 1995 and will continue doing so until the year 2000.
"Given the large size of the deal with the Serbian PTT, however, we will probably revise upwards these funds," he said.
The 675 million marks tagged to OTE's 20 percent stake in Telekom Srbija would not be a setback to the telecom's ambitious modernisation plans.
"The deal does not stand in the way of OTE's on-going investment programmes which are carried out according to schedule," Skarpelis said.

OTE is in the midst of an investment plan totalling 1,200 billion drachma by the year 2000 for widespread digitalisation of its trunk network, improvement of international networks and expansion of its product range.
A smaller 135 billion drachma Fast-Track investment plan for 1997 and 1998 is also being implemented to accelerate digitalisation.

OTE seeks to raise up to an estimated 200 billion drachmas through a 7.5 percent rights issue in the coming weeks, along with a part-flotation which includes a private placement with international institutional investors and a public offering. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
